messages:
Maria: Heads-up — CI perf alert on main after yesterday's api-proto merge. SSE tail latency up ~2.1x for 2-second windows on production-like load. https://ci.example.com/build/7421 :warning:

CI Bot: [perf-check] build 7421 failed perf thresholds for endpoint /stream (tail_latency_p95 increased from 110ms -> 240ms)

Ashwin: Any change in runtime kernels/kv cache or just API surface? Did we change chunking/flush?

Kai: I ran a flamegraph on a repro load. Top delta is serialization + write loop. Looks like extra stringify/validation in tool-calling shim. snippet:
```
async function callTool(t){
  const payload = JSON.stringify({meta, t}); // new
  await socket.write(payload);
}
```

Kai: Also noticed SSE buffering changed — proto now sets `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` + a small 16KB buffer in the muxer; flushes only on full chunk.

Natalie: Oof. That explains bursty tails. Any bisect candidate?

Ashwin: I did a quick git-bisect locally. Repro narrows to commit abc1234 (api-proto: multiplexing + validation middleware). Reverting that commit locally drops p95 back to ~115ms.

SRE Oncall: Can we hotfix by reverting the header change only? Or fast revert PR?

Maria: Let's do a revert PR and a canary rollback. I'll open PR and trigger canary. @deploy-bot can you hold canary until we patch validation?

deploy-bot: Canary queued for rollback: https://deploys.example.com/rollout/5678 - paused awaiting manual approval

Ashwin: Patch plan: remove middleware stringify, switch to streamed encoder, and adjust muxer to flush on newline boundary. Also add unit for SSE flush thresholds.

Kai: Will add microbench and a CI perf test for streaming latency (short sequences). CI currently only checks throughput so this slipped.

Natalie: Filed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-proto/pull/981 (revert abc1234) — added perf note and test

Maria: Great. Action items: 1) approve revert PR + canary rollback (Maria) 2) Ashwin/Kai add test + patch 3) SRE monitor p95 for 2h post-rollback.

SRE Oncall: Monitoring alerts will be in #incidents if p95 > 200ms. I'll leave notifications on.

Maria: Thanks all :thumbsup:
